title: Part (a): spectral-norm relative-error case unaddressed (only Frobenius proved)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Severity: scope / faithfulness (Part (a)).** The problem statement defines $A_k=\arg\min_{\mathrm{rank}(B)\le k}\|A-B\|$ "in spectral or Frobenius norm" and asks (a) for the sharp sketch-size threshold so that
$$\|A-A_k^{\mathrm{rand}}\|\le(1+\varepsilon)\|A-A_k\|$$
with matching lower bounds. As written this includes the **spectral-norm** case.

**Gap.** The submitted Part (a) theory is entirely Frobenius-norm: the HMT structural bound $\|A-P_YA\|_F^2\le\tau_k^2+\|\Sigma_2\Omega_2\Omega_1^\dagger\|_F^2$, the inverse-Wishart expectation $1+\frac{k}{p-1}$ (Thm `thm:lower`), and the PCP route (Thm `thm:pcp`) are all squared-Frobenius arguments. None of the existing gaps (G1–G6, issues rm-10086-2…7) address the spectral norm.

**Why this matters.** A relative-error **spectral-norm** $(1+\varepsilon)$ guarantee at the same sketch size $\ell=k+O(k/\varepsilon)$ is in general *false*. HMT's average spectral-norm bound is
$$\mathbb E\,\|A-P_YA\|_2\ \le\ \Big(1+\sqrt{\tfrac{k}{p-1}}\Big)\sigma_{k+1}+\frac{e\sqrt\ell}{p}\Big(\sum_{j>k}\sigma_j^2\Big)^{1/2},$$
whose second term is a multiple of the **tail energy** $\tau_k=\big(\sum_{j>k}\sigma_j^2\big)^{1/2}$, not of $\|A-A_k\|_2=\sigma_{k+1}$. For slowly decaying spectra $\tau_k\gg\sigma_{k+1}$, so the ratio $\|A-P_YA\|_2/\sigma_{k+1}$ cannot be forced below $1+\varepsilon$ by increasing $\ell$ alone — it is bounded below by $\sim\tau_k/\sigma_{k+1}$. Achieving a relative *spectral-norm* bound requires either a spectral-gap hypothesis or $q$-step power iteration (then the tail term is suppressed as $(\sigma_{k+1}/\sigma_j)^{2q}$).

**Required fix (one of).**
1. Explicitly **restrict Part (a) to the Frobenius norm**, and state that the spectral-norm relative-error guarantee at $\ell=k+O(k/\varepsilon)$ does not hold in general (with the $\tau_k/\sigma_{k+1}$ obstruction), OR
2. **Add the spectral-norm theory**: state a spectral-gap / numerical-rank hypothesis or introduce $q$ power-iteration steps and prove the HMT power-iteration spectral bound, then derive the corresponding sharp threshold and its matching lower bound.

Without one of these, the solution does not faithfully cover the spectral-norm case the problem explicitly allows.

(Numerical illustration: for $\sigma_j=j^{-0.15}$, $m=600,n=400,k=5$, $\ell=k+\lceil k/\varepsilon\rceil$, $\varepsilon=0.3$: basic randomized SVD gives Frobenius rel. error $\approx0.99\le1+\varepsilon$ but spectral rel. error $\approx1.21$ with tail/$\sigma_{k+1}\approx12$; the spectral ratio decreases only slowly with $\ell$. A sharper adversarial spectrum makes the $(1+\varepsilon)$ violation arbitrarily large.)
